This lets wallet, kernel and validation code report richer, mergeable error information instead of ad hoc output parameters.

result.summary: This PR extends util::Result to support returning a distinct failure value (not just a success value) and to accumulate multiple error and warning messages with a merge/Update() operation, shrinking the type's memory footprint in the process. It applies the new class to node::LoadChainstate and node::VerifyLoadedChainstate as a worked example, replacing the old tuple<status, bilingual_str> return type. It also adds a util/messages.h/.cpp module for error/warning message handling shared by the Result class, and touches kernel and wallet call sites mechanically to match the new interface. The PR has been open since 2022 and has undergone dozens of rebases and redesigns.
result.problem: Existing util::Result could only report a single error string, and functions like LoadChainstate needed a way to return distinct, actionable failure codes as well as descriptive messages, and to accumulate errors/warnings from nested calls. This blocked the intended broader use of Result in wallet-loading (#25722) and kernel/validation fatal-error propagation (#29700).

open_concerns: Whether util::Result's approach is redundant with, or should be built on top of, util::Expected/std::expected; hodlinator, arejula27 and maflcko have proposed alternative designs and the author has defended the current design at length without full consensus (agreed to disagree in places).
Whether the PR should simply be closed and reopened fresh given 300+ comments make review impractical (sedited, maflcko, 2026-05), which the author has not directly answered.
resolved_concerns: Missing explicit operator bool() regression fixed after sipa/hernanmarino flagged it.
Compiler warnings (missing-field-initializers, clang-tidy performance-no-automatic-move) fixed via targeted commits.
CI maybe-uninitialized false positive from this PR's own changes fixed with a CI flag tweak.
Early requests to split out interface-only changes were honored by spinning off #25721 and #29906.

result.card: This long-running (since 2022, 80+ force-pushes) refactor extends util::Result to carry structured failure values plus multiple mergeable error/warning messages, and applies it to node::LoadChainstate/VerifyLoadedChainstate as a worked example. Its main importance is as infrastructure: three other substantive PRs (#25722 wallet-loading errors, #29700 kernel fatal-error propagation, #26022 ResultPtr) explicitly depend on it and have been rebasing against it for years. Support is real (repeat ACKs from sedited, laanwj, achow101) but there is a long-standing, unresolved design debate over whether util::Expected/std::expected should be used instead, and most recently a repeat ACKer suggested closing and reopening the PR fresh because the 300+ comment thread makes review impractical, a suggestion the author has not yet addressed. The validation-side chainstate example itself is arguably weak motivation since it doesn't use Result's warning/multi-error features. No CI or merge blockers exist on the code itself, but review value is currently clouded by the closure suggestion.
